channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Iranian Regime Seeks To Reclaim Lion And Sun Symbol Embraced By Protesters
item.description: A senior Iranian official has claimed the Islamic republic owns the Lion and Sun emblem, a traditional symbol used by anti-regime protesters to express national pride and defiance of theocratic rule.

item.title: Wider Europe Briefing: The EU's New Sanctions On Russia And Previewing The NATO Defense Ministers' Meeting
item.description: What’s in the new EU sanctions package on Russia?

item.title: Seth G. Jones: Kremlin Trying Hard To 'Hide The Actual Number' Of Russian Troops Killed In Ukraine
item.description: The Kremlin has made "every effort" to hide the high number of deaths among Russian troops in Ukraine, where their slow advance has come at the cost of some 1.2 million casualties, Seth G. Jones of the CSIS think tank told RFE/RL in an interview about a new CSIS report.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan May Be First State Targeted Under EU Anti‑Circumvention Rules
item.description: Under a proposed 20th European Union sanctions package against Russia, expected to be adopted by the end of the month, Kyrgyzstan could face certain export restrictions for the first time.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Reshuffles National Security Leadership Amid Political Tensions
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov dismissed Kamchybek Tashiev as chairman of the State Committee for National Security (SCNS) on February 10 and appointed Jumgalbek Shabdanbekov as acting chairman amid rising political tensions in the Central Asian nation.

item.title: Vance Lands In Azerbaijan As Caucasus Peace Deal Visit Continues
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance arrived in Azerbaijan on February 10 as he continues a trip to the Caucasus aimed at shoring up support for a US-brokered peace deal with Armenia and to push a strategic transit corridor Washington sees as central to reshaping trade, energy, and influence in the region.

item.title: Russian Officer Deserted By Shooting Himself To Avoid Fighting In Ukraine
item.description: Russian officer Yevgeny Korobov participated in the invasion of Ukraine. Deciding to get out of there, he shot himself in the leg and ended up in the hospital. Korobov realized he did not want to return to the war and fled Astana, but officials refused to grant him refugee status.

item.title: Hailed As A War Hero, A Russian Officer Says He Shot Himself To Flee Ukraine
item.description: Yevgeny Korobov was hailed as a hero on Russian TV for his role in the country’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine -- but actually shot himself in the leg to escape the war and has now fled to Kazakhstan. Russia’s war, he says, is based on “a lie.”

item.title: EU Set To Blacklist Uzbek Cotton Pulp Firms Linked To Russian Military
item.description: The EU’s new sanctions target two Uzbek companies tied to businessman Rustam Muminov, who is sanctioned for supplying cotton pulp for Russian gunpowder and ammunition production. Evidence suggests his network dominates Uzbekistan’s cotton cellulose exports to Russia.

item.title: Amid Russian Strikes And Power Cuts, Ukraine Turns To Yurts And Plov
item.description: Central Asians living in Ukraine have brought some ancestral traditions to help those facing freezing winter and power cuts. Russian air assaults may have caused widespread power outages, but more cities are now featuring warm yurts and friendly hosts offering hot dishes from Central Asia.
